stop_condition: Every claim in plan:718-737 is traced to shipped behaviour I drove myself, both rollup axes are shown to decide independently, no new gate arm ships without a negative control, and no critical/high finding remains in the record-writing, record-reading or approve-refusal paths of either axis.

findings.evidence: reviewer_identity is interpolated RAW into token position 1 of the DESIGN-ROLLUP v1 machine prefix and is checked ONLY for emptiness (:16007). The sibling recorder cmd_design_review_record, which this region's own header says it copies verbatim, DOES guard the same field: assert_record_scalar 'design-review-record' "$tid" 'reviewer' "$reviewer_identity" at :10928, before building its record at :10948. Census: 0 assert_record_scalar calls anywhere in cmd_design_rollup vs 1 assert_record_model_scalar (for model). PROVEN against the shipped parser, not reasoned about: feeding latest_design_rollup's own capture regex a record built from reviewer_identity='design-claude model=x design_hash=<64hex> units=1/1 verdict=coherent gaps=0 at 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z: forged' while the REAL reviewer verdict was needs_revision yields {"reviewer":"design-claude","model":"x","design_hash":"<64hex>","units_have":"1","units_total":"1","verdict":"coherent","gaps":"0"}. The same crafted value is rejected by assert_record_scalar's own class test.
findings.description: A design-reviewer verdict can forge the two fields cmd_approve actually reads (verdict and design_hash), so DESIGN-ROLLUP-REFUSAL clears on an incoherent verdict. This is the bjx grammar-injection class the file's own guard exists for, and the class this branch's most recent commit (fed594c, 'a record can no longer impersonate the structure that reads it') closed elsewhere. The reviewer's output is untrusted by construction: the packet it reads contains the design artifact and a union diff, both project-content the orchestrator relays verbatim. FIX: add assert_record_scalar 'design-rollup' "$tid" 'reviewer' "$reviewer_identity" immediately before :16073, matching :10928. The legitimate literal design-claude passes that class unchanged, so the fix is zero-cost. Pair it with a negative control driving the crafted value through design-rollup and asserting reviewer_invalid_chars.

findings.evidence: MEASURED TWICE, standalone, no other load, at the working tree over HEAD 6de6c9e with DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools: run 1 `bash .claude/scripts/tests/design-rollup.test.sh` = 74/74, exit 0, 806.83s wall (zsh time: 351.25s user, 355.20s system, 87% cpu, 13:26.83 total); run 2 `/usr/bin/time -p bash .claude/scripts/tests/design-rollup.test.sh` = 74/74, exit 0, real 823.17 (user 357.17, sys 362.57). SPEC_TIMEOUT_S defaults to 900 (:1010). Worst measured 823.17s gives headroom 900/823.17 = 1.093x and 76.83s of margin.
findings.description: The new spec becomes the tier's worst-case standalone runtime, displacing unrecorded-review-artifact.test.sh at 771.35s, and both measurements are ABOVE the 800s split trigger run-tests.sh:999 already names ('e.g. split at 800s standalone, or at the next round that adds assertions to this file, whichever comes first'). The same change set edited that exact comment block (+119 lines, EXPECTED_SPECS 66 -> 68) without updating the worst-case figure or the 1.167x headroom ratio -- which is the failure mode the comment itself says has already happened 'twice now' (:968). run-tests.sh:1003-1005 records that ubuntu-latest is typically slower than the boxes these numbers were measured on, so the real CI margin is smaller than 76.83s. The implementer's own notes state the specs were run 'to their own natural completion ... never through run-tests.sh's watchdog', so the cap was never exercised. FIX: split design-rollup.test.sh (the natural seam is Sections A-H vs I-K, which own separate epics already), or raise SPEC_TIMEOUT_S and say what was measured -- and update the worst-case figure and ratio in the comment either way.

findings.evidence: The packet's union diff is `git diff [--stat] "$base...HEAD" -- <union files>` where base resolves via origin/HEAD then origin/main, origin/master, main, master. MEASURED on this repo for the three core files of this change set: `git diff --stat main...HEAD --` reports 14,532 insertions / 203 deletions and 997,254 bytes of content, while the ACTUAL uncommitted change set under review is 2,189 insertions / 9 deletions and 150,097 bytes. DESIGN_ROLLUP_DIFF_CAP_BYTES is 100,000 (:15335), so 997,254 is 9.97x the cap and the packet degrades to --stat only. In the test fixture the diff is EMPTY by construction, verified directly in a throwaway repo: `git init` leaves HEAD on main, base resolves to main, and `git diff --stat main...HEAD -- <file>` prints nothing after two commits. The only assertion touching this section is `grep -c '^### '` == 4 (design-rollup.test.sh:492-493).
findings.description: Three compounding problems in the one packet item plan:723-725 names as evidence for DS1/DS2. (a) WRONG SCOPE: base...HEAD is everything on the branch since it diverged from main, so a D6-scoped design's union diff sweeps in D1-D5; (b) BLIND TO THE WORK UNDER REVIEW: this workflow gates uncommitted working-tree changes (the change set is git-status-derived and approve binds it), and base...HEAD cannot see them at all -- the most recently completed unit is exactly the work most likely to still be uncommitted at packet time; (c) UNTESTED: no assertion ever observes a non-empty or non-degraded diff, and the fixture cannot produce one. design-reviewer.md:62 instructs the reviewer to 'Read the union diff and the completion contracts to check this directly', so the axis's substantive evidence is a --stat of the wrong scope with no content. The degradation note ('the per-unit F7 contracts above already list every touched path') is true about PATHS and silent about CONTENT, which is what DS1/DS2/DS8 need. FIX: derive the diff from the same evidence the gate already binds (HEAD plus working tree, scoped to the union file set), or from the design's own start point, and add an assertion that observes real diff content.

findings.evidence: The record path requires --design-hash to EQUAL the current governing design hash (:15856) AND to DIFFER from the prior record's design hash (:16048). Together those admit at most one DESIGN-ROLLUP verdict per design_hash, ever. approve requires the LATEST verdict to be coherent AND bound to the current design hash (:6724, :6730). Grep census: the entire DESIGN-ROLLUP-JUDGEMENT region (:15182-16077) contains ZERO references to change_set_hash, while both sibling judgement records bind one -- RUBRIC carries change_set_hash=<h> (:7920) and REVIEW-ARTIFACT carries reviewed_hash=<h> (:8641) -- and qa-gate.sh enter clears rubric-satisfied when the change set moves (:1891, :1903-1911).
findings.description: Two consequences, both from the same artifact-only binding. (a) A coherent verdict CANNOT GO STALE as implementation changes: the epic's own approve can re-run at any number of new change sets and the judgement leg keeps passing on a verdict formed before that work existed, because only the design document's hash is compared. DS8 is explicitly scoped to 'an anti-pattern can enter during implementation that was never visible in the design's own text' (design-reviewer.md:65), so the one criterion most sensitive to implementation content is the one the binding cannot track. (b) It also cannot be REFRESHED: a second verdict at the same hash is refused as a duplicate, so there is no way to re-judge after more work lands, and an incoherent verdict at hash H makes the governing task permanently unapprovable while H governs -- no bypass exists on this axis (region header; orchestrator.md 5f), and choose approve delegates to the same cmd_approve. The documented escape (orchestrator.md 5f: amend the artifact, a fresh Revision log row, a moved design_hash) forces a design-document edit even when the reviewer's gaps are purely implementation-side, which is the hash-moving no-op edit this arc has otherwise refused. FIX: bind the record to the change set as well as the artifact (the RUBRIC precedent), and allow a superseding verdict at the same design_hash when the change set has moved.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:14484-14488 (header), :14731-14735 (emitter), :14768-14796 (the unreachable consequence); CHANGELOG.md 'Four kinds of open issue'; docs/HOOKS.md:2181 'Four kinds of issue'
findings.evidence: Emitted kinds, counted from the shipped source (`sed -n '14498,15180p' qa-gate.sh | grep -oE '--arg k "[a-z_]+"' | sort -u`): ambiguous_unit_binding, hash_divergence, incomplete, tracker_diff_mismatch, undeclared_scope -- FIVE. CHANGELOG.md, docs/HOOKS.md:2181 and the task's own completion notes all say FOUR and enumerate the other four. `grep -rn ambiguous_unit_binding` over .claude/scripts/tests/, docs/ and CHANGELOG.md returns nothing: zero tests, zero documentation. Trace of the documented consequence: the FIRST child bound to a unit populates unit_task_map_json (:14736); a SECOND pushes the ambiguous issue and `continue`s (:14731-14734) WITHOUT clearing the map, so in CONDITION 1 mapped_task is non-empty (:14783-14785), the `[ -z "$mapped_task" ]` branch is skipped, and the is_ambiguous reason string at :14793 is unreachable except through a jq failure that empties the whole map.
findings.description: ambiguous_unit_binding is a shipped gate condition -- it raises the coherence count, which COHERENCE-ROLLUP-REFUSAL reads to refuse approve at exit 2 -- with no positive test, no negative control, and no UNPAIRED declaration. .claude/tests/README.md:534-537 states the requirement as a closeout obligation, not a preference: 'at closeout, every check added by the change is either paired to the standard below or listed as UNPAIRED with a reason.' The same file's Section 11 METatest shows the author knows the standard (narrow COHERENCE-COUNT-ROLLUP sentinels, END { if (!found) exit 7 }, specific misbehaviour, restore control, both scripts driven), so this is an omission rather than a capability gap. The header's claim that an ambiguous unit 'is ALSO counted incomplete (unresolved)' does not happen, and :14793 is dead code implying the author believed otherwise. The gate still fails closed (count >= 1), so no false pass. A second UNPAIRED-undeclared check ships alongside it: the reentrancy guard has only a wall-clock bound (F.3, elapsed < 30s) and no mutant, which is defensible -- a mutant would hang -- but is not declared.

findings.evidence: plan:721 specifies `gaps=[...]`; the shipped record emits `gaps=<n>` (:16073, gaps_count from `.required_fixes | length`). The justification given in all three places is that 'Neither record in this codebase stores an array verbatim in its machine prefix'. FALSIFIED against a live record: `bd show claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.7 --json --include-comments` returns `REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 iteration=8 reviewer=qa-claude model=claude-opus-5[1m] pin=claude-opus-5 reviewed_hash=... risk_threshold=high verdict=findings stopped_by=stop_condition findings=[R8-F1:medium,R8-F2:low,R8-F3:low,R8-F4:medium] artifact_hash=... at ...`, built at qa-gate.sh:8641 with a literal bracketed csv in the machine prefix.
findings.description: This is D6's deviation from the governing plan, and the whole rebuild was justified by 'the plan governs'. The ENGINEERING call is defensible on grounds the documents do not state: required_fixes are free-text sentences containing spaces and commas, and there is no gap-id space (unlike REVIEW-ARTIFACT's R<n>-F<n>), so a verbatim array genuinely would not survive a single-line token grammar. But the premise actually offered is false, and REVIEW-ARTIFACT is the precedent the plan's own shape matches. FIX: correct the justification in all three places to the real reason (no gap-id space; free-text elements), and record D6 as a deviation on claude-workflow-plugin-uwzv alongside D1/D2/D5 so the arc's divergence ledger is complete.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/design-rollup.test.sh:820-843 (Section K); repeated in run-tests.sh, CHANGELOG.md and docs/HOOKS.md
findings.evidence: The awk mutation is `/# DESIGN-ROLLUP-REFUSAL BEGIN/ { skip=1 } !skip { print } /# DESIGN-ROLLUP-REFUSAL END/ { skip=0 }` -- it removes the ENTIRE region (:6656-6737), all three refusal arms plus the history-unreadable guard. Four documents describe it as stripping 'only'/'ONLY' the hash-freshness comparison: the section header at :820 and comment at :824-827, run-tests.sh's EXPECTED_SPECS ledger, CHANGELOG.md, and docs/HOOKS.md. K.1's non-vacuity leg is a line-count comparison, which cannot distinguish a region strip from a narrower one.
findings.description: .claude/tests/README.md:543-549 requires leg 1 to prove 'the mutation landed WHERE IT WAS AIMED'. The mutation landed where the awk aimed, but not where the CHECK's stated aim is, and the two are not the same claim. The conclusion survives for this particular state -- with a record present and genuinely coherent, only the freshness arm can fire, so region-strip and arm-strip are observationally identical here -- but that argument is not made anywhere, and a reader auditing the pair is told something the code does not do. The sibling Section 11 in design-coherence.test.sh shows the right shape: dedicated inner sentinels (COHERENCE-COUNT-ROLLUP BEGIN/END) plus END { if (!found) exit 7 }. FIX: add inner sentinels around :6724-6729 and target those, or correct the claim in all four documents to 'the DESIGN-ROLLUP-REFUSAL region' and state why only the freshness arm can fire in this state.

findings.evidence: CONDITION 2 reads each unit's completion payload and VERIFIES it: disk_sha=$(sha256_file "$payload_file") compared against the record's payload_sha, `continue` on mismatch (:14862-14866). The packet builder reads the SAME files through the same latest_implementer_completion_record / completion_payload_path_for pair and embeds them with no sha256_file call at all.
findings.description: The region header claims the packet's ingredients are 'EXACTLY what compute_design_coherence already collects as a byproduct of its own per-unit resolution loop'. They are not: one leg is digest-verified and the other is not, so the packet can embed a completion contract whose on-disk bytes no longer match the digest the record binds -- in an evidence artifact a reviewer is asked to judge the system from. FIX: reuse the same verify-then-read sequence, or state in the packet that section 2 is unverified. Related, same file: CONDITION 2 skips verification entirely when the record carries no payload_sha token (:14864's `[ -n "$impl_sha" ] &&`), which over-trusts rather than under-counts.

findings.evidence: (a) :6662 states 'zero issue_type=epic rows exist' as the premise for reinterpreting plan:731's 'epic-typed task'. MEASURED: `bd list --all --json | jq '[.[].issue_type]|group_by(.)|map({(.[0]):length})|add'` returns epic: 23 (all closed; `bd list --type epic --json | jq length` = 0 open). (b) :6476-6487, in the same function, argues at length that exit 5 belongs to a different command's convention and 'reusing it here would put two unrelated meanings on one exit code'; :6722/:6728/:6734 then do exactly that. (e) design-rollup-status double-prefixes its observations: 'not applicable: not applicable: ...' (:15633 wrapping an OBS that already carries the prefix), reproduced live on this task.
findings.description: Five small factual/consistency defects in shipped comments and operator-facing output. None changes behaviour; (a) and (b) matter most because they are the stated justifications for two plan deviations, and a reader who checks them finds one false and one self-contradicting. The axis-applicability reinterpretation in (a) is a BETTER predicate than literal issue_type matching and should be kept -- only its cited reason needs replacing.
